# Judith Chapter 8 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_008_page_001.jpg

---

**8:1** That is when Judith heard. Judith — daughter of Merari son of Ox son of Joseph son of Oziel son of Elkiah son of Ananias son of Gideon son of Raphain son of Ahitub son of Elihu son of Eliab son of Nathanael son of Salamiel son of Sarasadai son of Israel.

**8:2** Her husband had been Manasseh — her own tribe, her own family. He was dead now, gone since the barley harvest.

**8:3** He had been standing in the field supervising the harvesters when the sun struck him on the head. They carried him to bed and he died in Bethulia, the city he called home. They buried him with his ancestors in the field between Dothan and Balamon.

**8:4** Judith had been a widow for three years and four months.

**8:5** She had pitched a tent on the roof of her house, wrapped sackcloth around herself, and worn nothing but widow's clothes every day since.

**8:6** She fasted every day of her widowhood — every day except the Sabbath eves and Sabbaths themselves, the new moon eves and new moons, the feasts, and the days of celebration for the house of Israel.

**8:7** She was breathtakingly beautiful. Her late husband Manasseh had left her wealth — gold and silver, servants and slaves, livestock and land. She had managed all of it herself, with full authority.

**8:8** Not a soul spoke a word against her. She feared God with her whole being.

**8:9** Now she heard what the people were saying against Uzziah — all the bitter complaints about the water shortage, all the anger. And she heard what Uzziah himself had said: that he had sworn on oath to surrender the city to the Assyrians in five days if no help came.

**8:10** She sent her maidservant — the woman who ran her entire household — to summon Uzziah, Chabris, and Charmis, the three city elders.

**8:11** They came, and she confronted them: "Listen to me, rulers of Bethulia. What you said to the people today is wrong. This oath you have made — this deal you have struck between yourselves and God — promising to hand the city over to the enemy unless the Lord rescues us within this deadline. It is wrong.

**8:12** Who do you think you are, putting God to the test today? Who appointed you to stand in God's place over your fellow human beings?

**8:13** You are testing the Lord Almighty. You will never understand him — not ever.

**8:14** You cannot even probe the depths of another human being's heart. You cannot read another man's thoughts. So how do you intend to search out God — the one who made all of this — and know his mind and track his purposes? Brothers. Do not make God angry.

**8:15** If he does not choose to help us within five days, that is his decision. He has the power to shelter us on whatever timetable he chooses — or to destroy us right in front of our enemies. Either way it is his.

**8:16** Do not try to bind the purposes of the Lord our God. God is not a man you can bully. He is not a person you can soften up with appeals.

**8:17** So let us wait for his rescue, and cry out to him for help. If it pleases him, he will hear us.

**8:18** Because in our generation — and even today — there is not a single tribe or family or town among us worshiping handmade gods. That was what our ancestors did in the old days —

**8:19** and for that they were handed over to slaughter, to looting, to catastrophic defeat before their enemies.

**8:20** We know no god but him. So we have every reason to trust he will not abandon us or our people.

**8:21** If we fall into captivity, so does all of Judea. The sanctuaries will be stripped bare. God will hold us accountable for every drop of blood spilled.

**8:22** The massacre of our people, the enslavement of our land, the destruction of everything we have inherited — he will bring all of it down on our heads wherever they scatter us, and we will be a disgrace and a shame to our captors.

**8:23** Our slavery will earn us no sympathy. The Lord our God will make it a humiliation.

**8:24** Brothers — let us show our people what we are made of. Our brothers and sisters need us. The sanctuary, the temple, the altar — all of it rests on us.

**8:25** On top of everything else, let us be grateful to the Lord our God. He is testing us, just as he tested our ancestors.

**8:26** Think of Abraham. Think of how God tested Isaac. Think of what Jacob went through in Mesopotamia while he was working for his uncle Laban.

**8:27** God did not send them into those fires to break them. He did not destroy them. His hand is a disciplining hand — he trains those who come close to him. He is shaping them, not crushing them.

**8:28** Uzziah answered her: "Everything you have said is right. There is nothing in it anyone can argue with.

**8:29** And frankly, this is nothing new from you. Everyone in this city has known your wisdom since you were a girl. Your heart has always been in the right place.

**8:30** But the people were completely desperate from thirst. They backed us into a corner. We gave them an oath and we cannot walk it back.

**8:31** Pray for us. You are a woman of deep faith. Ask the Lord to send rain and refill our cisterns, and we will stop fainting away."

**8:32** Judith said: "Listen carefully. I am going to do something — and it will echo through every generation of our people forever.

**8:33** Stand at the gate tonight, you and the elders, and let me out. Me and my maid. Before that deadline you set — before you would have handed over the city — the Lord will have delivered Israel through my hand.

**8:34** Do not ask me what I am doing. I will not tell you until it is done."

**8:35** Uzziah and the rulers said: "Go in peace. May the Lord God go ahead of you and bring vengeance on our enemies."

**8:36** They turned and left her tent and returned to their posts.
